summary: Ran genuinely differently-framed searches (founder-retrospective, press-coverage, empirical/survey-research, US-diocese-vendor, and EdTech-failure-mode searches) against all five target claims. Claim 1 (no faith-specific leader-first precedent): found a faith-specific non-institutional growth precedent (YouVersion's early organic/viral growth) but it is user-first, not leader-first as scoped -- complicates, does not overturn (confidence 0.35). Claim 2 (defer campus-ministry coalitions): no credible counter-evidence found after a genuinely different search strategy; an independent source (First Things) actually reinforces the infrastructure/scale advantage behind the deferral -- reported as a low-confidence counter-claim per the absence-is-a-valid-finding instruction (confidence 0.1). Claim 3 (relational outperforms digital in campus ministry): no direct comparative outcome study found; Barna Group data refines the binary toward a complementary framing rather than confirming or overturning outperformance; one low-reliability stats aggregator was found and explicitly rejected as not credible (confidence 0.25). Claim 4 (EdTech leader-first analog transfers cleanly): found genuine complicating evidence -- EdTech commentary documents both a champion-dependent scaling failure mode and a FERPA-triggered institutional-review chokepoint structurally similar to the doctrinal-safety gate the brief's Risks section only speculated about (confidence 0.45). Claim 5 (diocese material is compliance-only and UK-only): found US-context, persuasion-oriented vendor material (Flocknote diocese page) that partially contradicts the framing, though verification was limited by a blocked page fetch and no independent/denominational-body persuasion source was found (confidence 0.3). All five claims received a genuine, differently-angled search effort within two rounds; no target claim was unfalsifiable or unworkable as scoped, so no bounce was needed.
